A FEW USEFUL ANSWERS

Before
we talk.

You don’t need every answer to start a useful conversation.

Is Grade 9 too early to start planning?

It can be a useful time to explore interests and build a manageable approach to high school. The conversation can focus on what makes sense now, while leaving room for your child’s interests to develop.

Can we get help if our child is already in Grade 11?

The call can help you review where things stand and what deserves attention before senior year. The discussion starts with your child’s current preparation and questions.

Does my child need research mentorship?

Research mentorship is one option for exploring an academic interest through guided work. Its relevance depends on your child’s interests, readiness, and preparation needs.

Can we discuss SAT preparation?

Yes. You can discuss how SAT preparation may fit into your child’s broader preparation timeline and the colleges they are considering. Testing requirements vary, so each college’s current policy matters.

What happens if we need ongoing support?

The call can help identify which support may be relevant. SAT preparation and research mentorship can come first, with college application support following as appropriate. Any ongoing work is a separate next step.

Explore which support makes sense for your family.
